texts: good. the lighting is a past event with Coraline Ash as agent, the lantern as what was lit, the Harbor Station as the whole that lantern belongs to, and sundown, day 190 and Year 1 all recorded. Worth knowing: 'day 190 of Year 1' reuses the day-of-month term, so no content is lost but the engine cannot yet order your dates by day-of-year.

good. the lantern is the agent of a past burning and mire-essence is the non-specific stuff it burned (a bare kind rather than a particular batch), which is the right reading for a bare mass object here.
good. producing brings its object into existence, so the mist-light gets its own witness - that is exactly what lets the next sentence's 'the mist-light' refer back to it.
good. 'a handful' is recorded as a vague-quantity phrase on a nightmoth group, so the count stays exactly as vague as you wrote it and no number is invented.

mixed: the event itself is right (four moths counted at the lantern, past tense), but 'four nightmoths' is an indefinite, so it mints a second, unconnected moth group - the handful the mist-light attracted and the four counted end up as two separate sets, and the landing and thread-leaving below attach to the counted four only. If they are meant to be the same moths, write 'Coraline Ash counted four of the nightmoths at the lantern at the third watch.' Separately, 'the third watch' survives only as an opaque constant: its rank is not queryable and cannot be ordered against other times.
good. the group landing is a past event and the per-member rule correctly carries the past tense into each moth's own landing.

mixed: everything but one role is right - the threads are filed under the role for objects an action creates, destroys or changes, when leaving merely deposits them unchanged, so they should take the displaced-object role instead, and the same wrong role is copied into the per-member rule. Your sentence is unambiguous and no rewrite would help; the role test is ours to apply.

mixed: the collecting, its source, dawn, day 191 and Year 1 are all recorded, and 'a small heap' is correctly a heap of silken threads with its size on the heap itself - but 'a small heap of silken threads' is indefinite, so it becomes a brand-new group with no link to the threads the moths left two sentences earlier, breaking the chain from deposit to cauldron. Link them with a definite: 'Coraline Ash gathered the silken threads from the lantern into a small heap at dawn on day 191 of Year 1.'
good. carrying moves the threads without changing them, and Cauldron Hall is recorded as the destination with its name.

mixed: the boiling, Hesper, the threads, the day and the year are all right, but 'in sea-water in the first cauldron' becomes two co-equal location atoms, so nothing records that the sea-water was in the cauldron - stacked 'in' phrases only chain that way when both name places, and sea-water is a substance. Naming the water as the means keeps both facts distinct and queryable: 'Hesper boiled the silken threads with sea-water in the first cauldron on day 191 of Year 1.' 'The first cauldron' itself needs no change - the rank is carried as an ordinal.
good. forming is a change the essence undergoes, so the mire-essence is its affected participant, and 'by evening' is recorded as a deadline rather than as a point in time.
good. storing moves the essence unchanged into the clay vessel, and 'clay vessel' is kept whole with its genus (a kind of vessel) exposed.
good. the drawing reuses the same mire-essence witness minted two sentences earlier and records 'stored' as a property of it, so the chain from cauldron to vessel to drawing stays connected.
